title: Regexes in the Corefile are length-limited

detection.reason: regexes are Corefile values, which are not collected

remediation: From 1.14.0 regexes in rewrite rules (name/cname/rcode/ttl), template directives and the errors plugin's `consolidate DURATION REGEXP` are capped at 10000 characters (maxRegexpLen, b723bd94d) and a longer one is rejected at Corefile load. Real-world regexes are far below the cap; only generated ones need a look.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*(rewrite|template|errors)\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # printed rewrite/template/errors regexes are length-checked

title: kubernetes: API server calls are rate-limited

detection.reason: the client-go rate is a default inside the plugin

quote: plugin/kubernetes: Rate limits to api server
remediation: Very large clusters may see slower initial sync after 1.14.0 because the kubernetes plugin now throttles its own API calls; watch `coredns_kubernetes_dns_programming_duration_seconds` after the hop.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*kubernetes\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # the printed kubernetes block syncs under a client-side rate limit

title: rewrite now runs before acl

detection.reason: plugin order is fixed inside CoreDNS; the Corefile projection carries directive names only

quote: core: Reorder rewrite before acl to prevent bypass
remediation: ACL rules are evaluated against the REWRITTEN name from 1.14.2; acl blocks in a server block that also rewrites need their names re-checked.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*(acl|rewrite)\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a server block printing both acl and rewrite applies acl to the rewritten name

title: TLS max version and cipher list are now Go's defaults (the TLS 1.2 minimum stays)

detection.reason: what the peers negotiate is request-time behaviour

remediation: 1.14.5 (bc4343b08, plugin/pkg/tls) drops the fixed cipher-suite list and the TLS 1.3 maximum from every TLS config CoreDNS builds — the tls directive's listeners and the forward/grpc/etcd TLS clients — keeping TLS 1.2 as the minimum. This WIDENS what peers can negotiate; nothing that connected before stops. Only environments that audited the old fixed suite list need to re-check what is negotiated now.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*(tls|forward|grpc|etcd)\\b|^\\s*(tls|https|grpc)://")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed TLS endpoint or TLS-capable upstream negotiates Go's defaults from 1.14.5

title: hosts: unsupported-type fallthrough for names with an A/AAAA entry — automatic in 1.14.5/1.14.6, opt-in from 1.14.7

detection.reason: read from the option KEY names the agent extracts inside each Corefile plugin block of every kube-system ConfigMap whose name contains coredns (agent 0.4.58+; older agents leave this NOT_DETECTABLE) — keys only, never values; import lines are not followed

quote: queries for record types unsupported by the *hosts* plugin continue to the next plugin when `fallthrough` is configured, even if the queried name has an A or AAAA entry in the hosts data.
remediation: 1.14.5 made a hosts block with `fallthrough` pass TXT/HTTPS/SVCB/… queries for overridden names upstream (a split-horizon leak). 1.14.7 reverses it: such names answer NODATA again unless the block sets `fallthrough_unsupported` (which requires `fallthrough`; CoreDNS refuses to start otherwise). Landing on 1.14.7 or later nothing leaks unless you opt in — decide whether you want the opt-in. Landing on 1.14.5/1.14.6, expect the leak.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*hosts\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed hosts block with fallthrough is affected: leaks on 1.14.5/1.14.6, opt-in via fallthrough_unsupported from 1.14.7
coversNotes: plugin/hosts: Fall through unsupported query types
plugin/hosts: Make unsupported type fallthrough opt-in

title: hosts: a `*` owner name is a wildcard from 1.14.5 — existing entries change meaning

detection.reason: hosts data (the mounted hosts file or inline entries) is not collected; only the directive's presence is

remediation: From 1.14.5 (6805f6f8a) a hosts entry whose owner name starts with `*` (`192.168.1.10 *.example.com`) matches one additional label below it, like the file plugin's wildcards, instead of being a literal name. Entries already written that way silently start answering for every one-label child. Check hosts files and inline entries for `*` owner names.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*hosts\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed hosts block's data must be checked for * owner names, which become wildcards at 1.14.5

title: autopath now runs before acl (1.14.7)

detection.reason: plugin order is fixed inside CoreDNS; the Corefile projection carries directive names only

quote: plugin/acl: Fix autopath from bypassing acl checks
remediation: 1.14.7 (18a58b9e8, core/dnsserver/zdirectives.go) moves autopath ahead of acl — and ahead of cache, header, dnssec, minimal and template — so ACL rules now apply to the queries autopath generates. A server block loading both acl and autopath can start answering REFUSED to search-path queries it used to resolve; re-check the acl rules there.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*(acl|autopath)\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a server block printing both acl and autopath applies acl to autopath's queries from 1.14.7

title: local: every name under .localhost. is answered locally (1.14.5); the localhost.<domain> prefix form is deprecated

detection.reason: which names clients resolve is request-time behaviour; only the local directive's presence is collected

remediation: From 1.14.5 a server block loading `local` answers any query under `.localhost.` (RFC 6761) with loopback records instead of passing it to later plugins or upstreams. The legacy `localhost.<domain>` prefix handling stays on by default but is now deprecated — set `local { localhost_prefix off }` to keep only the RFC form, and check nothing relied on `*.localhost.` names resolving elsewhere.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*local\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed local block answers *.localhost. itself from 1.14.5

title: The image pins a numeric uid/gid for its nonroot user

detection.reason: pod securityContext is not in the collected projection

quote: core: Pin numeric uid/gid for the nonroot user
remediation: `runAsNonRoot: true` now passes kubelet's check without an explicit runAsUser; manifests that set a different runAsUser to work around it can drop it.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("coredns"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name): runAsUser=\(.spec.template.spec.securityContext.runAsUser // .spec.template.spec.containers[0].securityContext.runAsUser // "unset") runAsNonRoot=\(.spec.template.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot // .spec.template.spec.containers[0].securityContext.runAsNonRoot // "unset") hostPorts=\([.spec.template.spec.containers[].ports[]? | select(.hostPort != null) | .hostPort | tostring] | join(","))"'  # runAsUser=0 pins the old root behaviour and a hostPort below 1024 needs NET_BIND_SERVICE once the image runs as nonroot

title: forward: default connect attempts are capped

detection.reason: retry counts are a default inside the plugin

remediation: Upstreams that needed many connect retries surface as errors sooner from 1.14.7; set `max_connect_attempts` (1.13.2+) explicitly if the old behaviour is needed.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*forward\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed forward retries connections a bounded number of times

title: TSIG is fully verified on DoH, DoH3, DoQ and gRPC transports

detection.reason: which clients sign with TSIG over which transport is request-time behaviour

remediation: Signed queries arriving over DoH/DoH3/DoQ/gRPC were previously not checked; from 1.14.3 a bad or unknown-key TSIG on those transports is rejected like it already was on UDP/TCP. Check clients that sign over encrypted transports use a configured key.
